Acidic solutions have a greater concentration of hydronium ions than hydroxide ions [ev_003], and at 25 °C acidic solutions have pH below 7 [ev_005]. Therefore the correct pair is pH = 2.4 and pOH = 11.6 [ev_001]. A pH of 11.6 would indicate a basic solution at 25 °C, which contradicts vinegar's acidity [ev_005]. The pH is the quantity normally measured directly with a pH meter, whereas the pOH is not usually measured because it is easily calculated from an experimentally determined pH value [ev_001].
